intro.title: About Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt
intro.description: Welcome to Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt, widely recognized as the town's classic Aussichtspunkt Hallstatt viewing point. Located along the lakeside road at Gosaumühlstraße 67 in Hallstatt, Upper Austria, Austria, this lookout offers the world-famous postcard panorama across Lake Hallstatt, framed by the Gothic Evangelical Parish Church spire, terraced timber houses and the Dachstein Alps. To be clear: this page refers to exactly this classic lakeside postcard viewpoint at Gosaumühlstraße 67; the Salzwelten salt-mine Skywalk platform high above the town is a separate attraction and is not covered here.
intro.nearbyText: When visiting Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt, you can easily combine the lookout with surrounding landmarks and points of interest, including the Market Square (Marktplatz) and the Charnel House in the old town, as well as the Salzwelten Hallstatt salt mine with its Skywalk viewing platform across the bay.

visitGuide.title: Visiting Tips
items: Best shooting time: morning light offers clear reflections; afternoon and evening tend to be backlit.
The viewing spot is very small and sits right next to the road, so watch the traffic at all times.
Respect resident privacy: do not make noise, enter private property or fly drones in the residential area.
Arrive before 9:00 am or after 5:00 pm to avoid tour-bus crowds at this compact stop.

alsoKnownAs.title: Why It Is Famous
items: Postcard View: the most photographed angle of Hallstatt, seen in countless travel features.
World Heritage: lies at the heart of the Hallstatt-Dachstein/Salzkammergut UNESCO Cultural Landscape (1997).
Lake & Alps: sweeping views over Lake Hallstatt towards the Dachstein massif.
Easy to reach: only a short, flat walk from the Market Square and the ferry landing.

sections.title: World Heritage
sections.content: The viewpoint looks out over the Hallstatt-Dachstein/Salzkammergut Cultural Landscape, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1997. The settlement sits on one of Europe's oldest salt-trading routes, with 7,000 years of mining history beneath the surrounding mountains.

sections.title: Traditional Architecture
sections.content: From the northern shore you see Hallstatt's timber-fronted houses climbing the mountainside, crowned by the spire of the Evangelical Parish Church. The compact old town is car-free, with painted facades and narrow lanes that are part of the protected heritage ensemble.

sections.title: Seasons & Light
sections.content: In calm weather the lake mirrors the church spire and the peaks - best enjoyed in the early morning. Autumn colours and winter snow transform the scene, while summer brings the largest crowds to this famous viewpoint.

sections.title: Salt, Name & Prehistory
sections.content: Hallstatt takes its name from the Old High German word 'hall' meaning salt – for centuries the 'white gold' of the region. After graves were discovered in 1846 in the high valley above the town, archaeologists named Europe's oldest Iron Age culture after this site: the Hallstatt culture (c. 800–450 BC).

hours.title: Opening Hours
hours.outdoorTime: Open 24 hours, free of charge all year round
hours.summerTime: Open all day; boat and ferry tours run seasonally
hours.winterTime: Open daily, hours vary by season (usually 09:30-16:30); check the official website
hours.warningTime: The viewpoint stands directly beside the busy lakeside road. Keep off the carriageway, watch for traffic, never block residents' driveways, and do not fly drones over private property.
hours.tip: Calm mornings give the clearest mirror reflections of the church spire and the Dachstein peaks, so sunrise until around 9:00 am is the most peaceful window.

tickets.title: Ticket Information
tickets.childrenPrice: Ferry fare across the lake; parking P1/P2/P3 outside the town is charged by the hour
tickets.cardPrice: The old town is car-free - reach the viewpoint on foot from the ferry landing, the Market Square or the Gosaumühle bus stop.

transport.title: Transportation
transport.airportDesc: The nearest airports are Salzburg Airport (SZG), about 80 km / 1.5 hours by road, and Vienna International Airport (VIE), about 290 km / 3.5 hours. From either airport, take a train to Hallstatt via Attnang-Puchheim or Bad Ischl.
transport.selfDriveDesc: Drive to Hallstatt and leave your car in the public parking lots P1, P2 or P3 outside the town - the centre is car-free for visitors. From P1 Gosaumühle the viewpoint is only about a 5-minute walk along the lake; from P2/P3 walk about 15 minutes along the lakeside promenade.
transport.busDesc: Classic route: take bus 150 from Salzburg to Bad Ischl, change to the train to Hallstatt Bahnhof, then take the ferry (or walk) across the lake to the town dock. From the dock, walk north along the lake for about 5 minutes to reach the viewpoint.
transport.intercityDesc: Obertraun on the far shore is a good base: park there and cross to Hallstatt by ferry or local bus to avoid the busy parking lots in peak season.
transport.cyclingDesc: The lakeside roads around Hallstatt are popular with cyclists. Once you enter the town, dismount and push your bike, as lanes are narrow and crowded with pedestrians.
transport.tipsDesc: The viewpoint sits at Gosaumühlstraße 67, a 5-10 minute walk from the Market Square. Walk north along the lakeside; when you see a cluster of visitors with cameras beside the road, you have reached the classic postcard position.

route.title: Visiting Route
steps: Start at the ferry landing or the Gosaumühle bus stop and walk into the old town.
Stroll through the Market Square (Marktplatz) and admire the colourful painted houses.
Walk north along the lakeside promenade and the Gosaumühlstraße for about 5-10 minutes.
Arrive at Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt and capture the classic postcard photo.
On the way back, visit the Evangelical Parish Church and the Charnel House (Beinhaus).
Take the funicular up to the Salzwelten salt mine and the Skywalk for a bird's-eye panorama.
supplements: The viewpoint is narrow and borders the carriageway, so watch the traffic while taking photos.
Respect local residents: no loud noise, no drones and no entry to private gardens.
Arrive before 9:00 am to have the viewpoint to yourself before the tour groups.

photoSpots.title: Photo Spots & Tips

spots.name: The Postcard Viewpoint
spots.desc: Stand at the roadside rail at Gosaumühlstraße 67 and frame the church spire, the timber houses and the lake reflection in one shot.

spots.name: Lakeside Promenade
spots.desc: Lower viewpoints along the shore capture the town mirrored in calm water, with swans and wooden boats.

spots.name: Market Square (Marktplatz)
spots.desc: Colourful historic facades and the Trinity column make for vivid close-range architecture shots.

spots.name: Skywalk Viewing Platform
spots.desc: Ride the funicular above the town for a sweeping aerial view over Hallstatt, the lake and the Dachstein range.

photoSpots.tipsContent: Morning light is best: the surface of the lake is calm and the reflections crisp. Afternoons are usually backlit, and because the platform is tiny, plan to arrive before 9:00 am to avoid tour-bus crowds.

hotels.title: Accommodation & Dining

hotels.name: Lakeside Guesthouses in Hallstatt
hotels.desc: Historic timber guesthouses in the centre offer an unforgettable stay above the lake - book months ahead for summer.
hotels.price: Very limited and expensive in peak season

hotels.name: Obertraun (opposite shore)
hotels.desc: A quiet, well-priced base across the lake, connected to Hallstatt by ferry and local bus.
hotels.price: Best-value alternative when Hallstatt is full

hotels.name: Bad Ischl (the Salzkammergut hub)
hotels.desc: The elegant spa town where the train from Salzburg stops, about 30-40 minutes from Hallstatt by train and bus.

hotels.supplementsContent: Around the lake, restaurants serve freshly caught fish from the Hallstätter See, such as grilled Reinanke, alongside Austrian classics such as schnitzel and knödel. For the best value, dine outside the immediate tourist centre.

items.name: Anna K.
items.text: The classic postcard spot! I arrived just after sunrise and had the mirror reflection of the church almost to myself. Tiny area, but absolutely magical.

items.name: Lukas M.
items.text: This is why Hallstatt is on every bucket list. The view over the lake to the fairy-tale town is unreal, even when it is cloudy.

items.name: Sarah W.
items.text: Iconic and very photogenic, but the spot is right on the road and tour groups arrive constantly. Go very early or late in the day and take care with cars.

items.name: David T.
items.text: Beautiful evening walk along the lakeside road from the Market Square. The viewpoint itself is small but the whole promenade is lovely.

items.name: Elena R.
items.text: Being inside a UNESCO landscape shows in every direction you look. The combination of lake, mountains and historic rooftops is stunning.

items.name: Martin B.
items.text: Great perspective of the church spire and houses. Note it is on a busy road and parking in town is not allowed - use P1 and walk.

items.name: Julia H.
items.text: Came in winter and the snow made everything look like a Christmas card. Quiet, crisp air, few people - highly recommended.

items.name: Stefan P.
items.text: Worth the trip for photographers, but respect the residents - the spot sits right beside their homes. Best before 9 am.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Quick answers about Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt

items.q: Where is Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt located?
items.a: Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt is located at Gosaumühlstraße 67 along the lakeside road on the northern edge of Hallstatt, in Upper Austria, Austria. It is a short 5-10 minute walk north of the Market Square.

items.q: Is the viewpoint free to visit?
items.a: Yes. Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt is an open roadside viewpoint beside a public road, so it is free to visit and accessible 24 hours a day all year round.

items.q: What is the best time to take the classic postcard photo?
items.a: Early morning (before about 9:00 am) is best: the lake is calm, the reflections of the church spire are crisp and the tour-bus crowds have not yet arrived. Afternoons are usually backlit.

items.q: How do I get to the viewpoint from Salzburg?
items.a: Take bus 150 from Salzburg to Bad Ischl, then the train to Hallstatt Bahnhof, then the ferry across the lake to the town dock. From the dock walk north along the lake for about 5 minutes. By car, park in P1/P2/P3 outside the town and walk.

items.q: Is there parking near the viewpoint?
items.a: The old town is car-free. Use the public parking lots P1 (Gosaumühle), P2 or P3 outside the town; P1 is only a short walk from the viewpoint. Parking is charged per hour.

items.q: Are there toilets, cafes or other facilities nearby?
items.a: The viewpoint itself has no facilities, but public toilets, cafes, restaurants and shops are a 5-10 minute walk away in the town centre, near the Market Square and the ferry landing.

officialManagement.title: About Panoramic Viewpoint - Hallstatt
officialManagement.text: The viewpoint is located within the Hallstatt-Dachstein/Salzkammergut UNESCO Cultural Landscape. The surrounding lakeside area and historic centre are administered by the Municipality of Hallstatt under the planning protection of the Province of Upper Austria and the Austrian Federal Monuments Office (BDA).

facilities.title: On-site & Nearby Amenities
facilities.subtitle: The viewpoint is an open, unstaffed scenic overlook with no on-site facilities. The list below describes the general types of services found in Hallstatt and along the lakeside – for planning only.
facilities.note: For planning only – general service types, not a recommendation of any specific business. Availability and opening hours change with the seasons; please check locally.

items.detail: Free and paid public toilets are located along the lakeside promenade and near the boat / tourist jetties in Hallstatt.
Paid public parking areas at the southern entrance of Hallstatt (around Lahn) are the closest option for drivers; parking is not permitted in the historic centre.
Traditional restaurants, lakeside cafés and small snack bars line the promenade and the pedestrianised centre.
Hotels, guesthouses and holiday apartments are available in Hallstatt and in Obertraun on the opposite side of the lake.
A small supermarket as well as shops for groceries, drinks and souvenirs operate in the centre of Hallstatt.
Petrol stations and public charging points for electric cars are available in Obertraun and along the Salzkammergut road network.
Cash machines are available in Hallstatt centre; card payment is widely accepted in restaurants and shops.
The Hallstatt tourist information office provides maps, hiking routes and boat schedules for the lake area.

advice.outfitSun: Clear skies: light clothes work well; keep a thin layer for the lakeside breeze.
advice.outfitSnow: Snowfall: warm winter coat and non-slip footwear.
advice.outfitUv: Strong UV – protect your skin and eyes.
advice.planSunny: Clear weather is best for the viewpoint: calm lake reflections in the morning and easy lakeside strolls.
advice.planCloudy: Soft, diffused light – great for photos and a full day outdoors along the lake without harsh sun.
advice.planRainProb: High rain chance: keep outdoor plans flexible and have an indoor backup ready.
advice.planRainLight: Light rain: the panorama looks muted, but a walk is still fine with an umbrella.
advice.planNoOutdoor: Not a great day outdoors: boats/ferries and the salt-mine cable car may pause – favour indoor sights.
advice.planWind: Strong wind may change boat schedules; the viewpoint itself is exposed and cool.
advice.planHot: Avoid long outdoor hours around noon – early morning or evening is far more comfortable.
advice.planFog: Dense fog: the view is severely limited and ferries may run late.
advice.planSnow: Snowy day: footpaths and mountain trails can ice over; the cable car may pause at short notice.
advice.gearRaincoat: Raincoat (skip the long umbrella in wind)
advice.riskRainHeavy: Heavy rain: avoid stream valleys, gullies and low lakeside ground; watch your step on wet paths.
advice.riskThunder: Thunderstorms: do not stay on the open lakeside, summits or under trees – postpone the cable car and hikes.
advice.riskWind: Gale-force wind: keep away from jetties, billboards and loose objects; ferries/boats may suspend service.
advice.riskFog: Fog: poor visibility for driving and walking; ferries may be delayed.
